transcript.content: Hi, it's good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Hi, Doctor. It's really nice to meet you, too. Um... I hope I'm in the right place. I'm just here because, well, I've been feeling a little overwhelmed lately. I've been trying to get to the bottom of something for about a year now, and I just want to make sure I'm doing the right thing, you know? 

It's about my dad's lab results. I work as a phlebotomist, so I know my way around a chart, and... well, I know someone in the clinic system has been altering or hiding parts of his bloodwork. I've tried to show my family and his doctors, but they keep telling me the numbers are perfectly fine. I don't want to be a bother to anyone, really I don't, but I know what I saw, and the chart just doesn't match. It's just been wearing me down so much, trying to prove it. Does that make sense? I hope that's an okay reason to be here.
Have you been hearing voices when no one else is around?

Oh, no. No, definitely not. I haven't experienced anything like that. I know me coming in here and talking about hidden lab results probably sounds a little... well, I don't want you to think I'm making things up or losing my grip. My mind is completely clear, I promise. 

I don't hear voices or anything scary like that. I'm just looking at the actual numbers on the screen at work and seeing the discrepancies with my own eyes. Does that answer your question? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right information.
Have there been times when you felt unusually energetic and needed much less sleep than usual?

Oh, um, no... no, I haven't really felt like that. I mean, I might stay up a little late sometimes trying to cross-reference my dad's old charts with the new ones, just to make sure I have all my facts straight before I talk to his doctor again... but I definitely still need my sleep. 

I'm not, like, bouncing off the walls or staying up for days on end or anything like that. I'm just trying to be thorough, you know? I hope that's the right kind of answer... I just want to be really honest with you so you know I'm thinking clearly. Is that what you meant by unusually energetic?
Do you believe for certain that someone in the clinic system is altering or hiding your dad’s lab results?

Um... well, I really don't want to sound stubborn or difficult. I respect the doctors so much, and I know my family means well when they keep telling me the numbers are fine. I always try to listen to them because I really don't want to cause any trouble for anyone. 

But... yes. I do believe it for certain. I've been trying to prove it for the past year now, that someone in the system is changing or holding back parts of his results. No matter how many people tell me everything is normal, I just... I know the chart doesn't match what I originally saw. 

I really hope you don't think I'm being unreasonable or difficult. It's just wearing me down so much, carrying this around and trying to get someone to see it. Does that make sense? I just want to be a good daughter and make sure he's safe. I hope it's okay that I'm being this honest with you... I just want to make sure I'm doing the right thing.
Aside from your dad’s lab results, do you believe anyone is trying to harm, monitor, or deceive you?

Oh, no, no. Nothing like that at all. I mean, I know how all this must sound, and I really don't want you to think I'm... well, paranoid or anything. 

Nobody is following me or trying to hurt me or anything scary like that. It's really just this one specific thing with my dad's charts at the clinic. Everything else in my life is completely normal, I promise. I go to work, I do my job—I'm a phlebotomist, so I'm around medical stuff all day, and I get along great with everyone there. 

I'm not suspicious of people in general, you know? I just... I just want to figure out this one issue with the lab numbers. I hope that shows that I'm keeping things in perspective. Is that the kind of thing you were asking about? I just want to make sure I'm giving you a clear picture of how I'm doing.
Do you find yourself repeatedly checking your dad’s lab records over and over, even when you try not to?

Oh, um, no... not like that. I mean, I don't feel like I have to keep looking at them when I don't want to, like a compulsion or anything. I know that would probably seem a little... well, obsessive, and I really try hard not to act like that. 

I do look at the records, of course, just to stay updated and make sure my notes are right, but it's really only when I need to prepare for a doctor's visit or if I'm organizing my files. I'm definitely not sitting there refreshing the patient portal all day or doing it against my will. 

I just want to be a helpful advocate for him, you know? Not a nuisance to anyone. I hope that answers your question... I just want to make sure you know I have good control over my actions. Does that make sense?
Have you noticed yourself becoming much less interested in being around other people than you used to be?

Oh, no, definitely not. I really try to make an effort to be social, you know? I wouldn't want you to think I'm just... hiding away at home or isolating myself or anything like that. 

I still love seeing my friends, and I chat with the patients and the nurses at work all the time. I'd hate to be antisocial or make people feel like I don't value them. I mean... maybe I'm a little tired sometimes just from worrying about my dad's situation, but I definitely haven't lost interest in people. I still really enjoy their company. 

I hope that's a good sign? I really just try to keep everything as normal and friendly as possible so I'm not a burden on anyone.
Has your certainty that someone is altering or hiding your dad’s lab results been present continuously for more than three months?

Um, yes... I suppose it has been a little longer than three months. I really hope that doesn't make me sound stubborn or like I can't let things go, but... it's actually been about a year. 

It started right around the time his medical problems began, when he first started needing all those frequent labs and appointments. I just want to be a good daughter, you know? I've been trying so hard to be patient and work with the clinic this whole time because I really don't want to be one of those difficult, complaining family members. But yes, it's been going on for about a year since I first noticed the numbers weren't matching up. 

I hope it's okay that I've been keeping track for that long? I just want to make sure I'm doing the right thing for him and being helpful.
Have you ever felt that your thoughts were being put into your mind or taken out of your mind by someone or something?

Oh, goodness, no. No, definitely not. My thoughts are just... they're just my own. 

I know I probably sound a little intense sometimes when I talk about the clinic and the lab numbers, but it's really just my own normal worrying, you know? Nobody is putting thoughts in my head or taking them away or anything scary like that. I really hope you don't think I'm... well, losing touch with reality or anything. I promise I'm completely clear-headed. 

I'm really just trying to use my background at work to be a good advocate for my dad. I hope that's okay? I just want to reassure you that my mind is completely my own and I'm totally in control of my thoughts.
Has anything about your dad’s lab results ever made you believe something impossible was happening, rather than something that could happen in real life?

Oh, no, no, nothing impossible. I mean, I know it sounds like a lot, but everything I'm talking about is... well, it's something that could actually happen in a clinic setting. 

I'm a phlebotomist, so I know how labs work, and I know that files can be altered or numbers can be changed by someone who has access to the system. It's not magic or aliens or... or anything crazy like that. I really want to make sure you know I'm being logical about this. It's just people doing things they shouldn't be doing with medical records. 

I hope you don't think I'm making up wild, impossible stories? I'm really just looking at the facts of what's happening in the real world. Does that make sense? I just want to be sure I'm explaining it in a way that sounds reasonable.
Have you ever seen things that other people could not see?

No, I've never had anything like that happen. I've never seen things that aren't there. 

I know sometimes when people get really stressed or worried about a family member, they might... well, maybe their imagination plays tricks on them? But that hasn't happened to me at all. I only see what everyone else sees—the actual printed reports, the computer screens at the clinic, the numbers right there in black and white. 

I hope you believe me? I really want to be clear that I'm completely grounded. I wouldn't want you to think I'm having hallucinations or anything like that, because I'm definitely not. Everything I'm seeing is completely real and physical. Is it okay that I'm being so firm about that? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right picture of how I'm doing.
Has this situation with your dad’s lab results caused serious problems for you at work, in your relationships, or in your day-to-day life?

Oh, um... well, I wouldn't say *serious* problems. I really try to be easy to get along with, I promise. But... I guess there have been a few little bumps? 

Just... well, my family has started sort of leaving me out of some of the appointment planning for my dad lately. I think they just don't want to stress me out, or maybe I was just asking too many questions about the charts. And... at work... I've always been a really good, dedicated employee, but lately I feel like I'm no longer being considered for lab supervision. I think... well, maybe some people there think I make the record issues a bit too confrontational. 

I really don't mean to be difficult, I just care so much about getting things right and keeping the patients safe. I hope you don't think I'm causing trouble or being a bad daughter? I'm really just trying to do the right thing and fix the mistakes I'm seeing... I hope you can understand where I'm coming from?
Before all this started with your dad’s lab results, did you generally have a long-standing tendency to distrust other people’s motives?

Oh, um... no, definitely not. I've actually always been... well, I like to think I'm a very trusting person. I really try to see the best in everyone, I promise. 

I've never been the type to, you know, assume people have bad intentions or anything like that. I've always had great relationships with my coworkers and my friends, and I usually just take people at their word. I hope you don't think I'm just a naturally suspicious or negative person? Because I'm really not. 

This whole thing with the clinic and the records... it's really just because the proof is right there in front of me, not because I was looking for a reason to doubt anyone. Usually, I'm very easygoing and open. Does that make sense? I just want to make sure you know I'm normally a very agreeable person.
Outside of this issue with your dad’s lab results, have you been functioning pretty much normally in your daily life?

Oh, yes, definitely. I mean, I try really hard to make sure everything else is completely normal. 

Outside of the... well, the disagreement over the records, I'm still doing everything I'm supposed to do. I still go to all my phlebotomy shifts, and I'm always on time. I pay all my bills, keep the house clean, take care of myself... you know, just regular day-to-day things. I haven't let any of that slip at all. 

I really want to show that I'm responsible and capable, you know? I hope that shows that I'm handling things well overall? I just don't want you to think my whole life is falling apart or anything, because I really am keeping up with all my normal responsibilities. Is it okay that I'm still working and doing everything else like usual?
When this first started, did your certainty that someone was altering your dad’s lab results come on very suddenly—within about two weeks?

Oh, um... suddenly? I... well, I don't think it was like a light switch, you know? I really try not to jump to conclusions about things like that. 

I think it was more... gradual? Like, I just started noticing little inconsistencies over time when I was looking at his charts. I didn't just wake up one day and decide someone was doing it on purpose, I promise. I really wanted to give everyone the benefit of the doubt at first. It just sort of... built up over a few months as I kept seeing more and more things that didn't match up. 

I hope that's the right answer? I just want to make sure you know I wasn't being rash or making wild accusations out of nowhere. I really took my time to be sure. Does that sound reasonable to you?
Has anyone told you that your speech or your thoughts seem disorganized or hard to follow?

Oh, no, no one has ever said anything like that to me. I... I really try to be very clear when I communicate, especially at work. 

I mean, I know sometimes when I try to explain the... the issues with the lab results, there's just so much data to go through, and maybe I get a little too detailed? But I always make sure I'm making sense. I would hate it if people thought I was rambling or confusing. I'm very careful about how I present things. 

My thoughts are very organized, I promise. I even keep a binder so I can show people exactly what I mean in a logical way. I hope I've been making sense to you today? I really try my best to be easy to understand.
During this past year, have you had a period of at least two weeks when you felt depressed most of the day nearly every day?

Oh, no, definitely not. I mean, I try really hard to stay positive, you know? 

I haven't felt depressed like that at all. Of course, it's been a little stressful dealing with everything regarding my dad, but I always make sure to keep a smile on my face and push through it. I wouldn't let myself get down for weeks at a time. I have too many responsibilities at work and at home to let that happen. 

I really try to be an upbeat person. I hope I don't seem depressed to you? I've been doing my best to handle everything with a good attitude, I promise. I just want to make sure I'm doing things right.
Have you had a period where you felt emotionally flat or unable to express much feeling?

Oh, no, I wouldn't say that at all. I think I'm actually a very expressive person, you know? 

I mean, as a phlebotomist, I have to be warm and reassuring with my patients all day. You can't really do that if you're emotionally flat, right? I always try to show people that I care and that I'm present with them. I've never felt like I couldn't express my feelings. If anything, I'm probably a little too empathetic sometimes! 

I really try to be an open and warm person. I hope I'm coming across that way to you? I definitely don't feel numb or anything like that. I feel things very normally, I assure you.
